<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Financial Summary:    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The significant factors affecting our results for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2011, were:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The increase in net revenues of $61.9&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to the prior
year, was primarily due to the opening of our gaming facility at Scioto Downs. This increase was offset in part by decreases in net revenues at Presque Isle Downs and to a lesser extent, Mountaineer,
which were attributable to increased competition in Ohio. </FONT></DD></DL>
<UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>All
of our properties experience varying competitive pressures, from casinos in western Pennsylvania, western New York, northern West Virginia and eastern Ohio. We believe the expansion of gaming in
Ohio, which includes a casino that opened in Columbus in October 2012 and additional casinos in Cincinnati and Toledo, as well as the installation of VLTs at existing horse race tracks including
ThistleDown and Northfield Park, which are both located in the Cleveland area, and the potential relocation of a racetrack to Austintown, will have a negative impact on our results of operations at
all our properties and such impact may be material. We intend to be proactive in our efforts to mitigate the effects of such competition, which include expanding marketing initiatives and proactively
managing our costs structures at our properties. Information regarding litigation seeking to prevent gaming activities in Ohio is discussed in detail in Part&nbsp;I, Item&nbsp;3. "Legal
Proceedings" above. </FONT></P>

</UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>Project opening expenses in 2012 of $2.7&nbsp;million associated with the opening of our Scioto Downs gaming facility. </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>The increase of $7.8&nbsp;million in interest expense for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, compared to the prior
year was due to the August 2011 refinancing where we issued $565&nbsp;million 11.5% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes and whose proceeds were used to refinance our former debt obligations and finance
development of the Scioto Downs gaming facility. The increase was partially offset by $1.3&nbsp;million of capitalized interest related to the construction of our gaming facility at Scioto Downs. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="dm44201_financial_results_for_the_year__fin03060"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_dm44201_3"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>  <A NAME="financial"></A>Financial results for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011    <BR>    </I></B></FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="dm44201_net_revenues"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_dm44201_4"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B>  Net Revenues    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, comprised of $456.2&nbsp;million in gaming and pari-mutuel
revenues (93% of total net revenues), $47.9&nbsp;million of non-gaming revenues (10% of total net revenues) less $14.1&nbsp;million of promotional allowances (-3% of total
net revenues), increased $61.9&nbsp;million, or 14.5%, compared to net revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, comprised of $395.5&nbsp;million in gaming and pari-mutuel
revenues (92% of total net revenues), $43.7&nbsp;million of non-gaming revenues (10% of total net revenues) less $11.1&nbsp;million of promotional allowances (-2% of total
net revenues). The increase was primarily attributable to the following components. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Gaming  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming revenues are comprised of the net win from our slot operations, table games and poker. Gaming revenues for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2012 of $445.8&nbsp;million represents a $60.5&nbsp;million, or 15.7%, increase compared to the prior year. The increase of $60.5&nbsp;million is comprised of an increase in
slot and poker revenue of $69.0&nbsp;million and $0.4&nbsp;million, respectively, offset by a decrease </FONT></P>

competition within our target market, including the opening of the Cleveland casino. We attribute the slot revenue increase to Mountaineer's continued disciplined marketing approach, which included

opened in Columbus, Ohio and, as expected, we have seen a decline in our gaming revenues at Scioto Downs. We believe the opening of the additional casino will be a catalyst in growing the gaming
revenues for the Columbus region to levels consistent with other markets of its size. We will continue to be proactive in our efforts to grow our revenues and customer database to maintain a share of
the market while managing our expenses in order to maximize margins. </FONT></P>

simulcast signals from/to other race tracks. Pari-mutuel commissions for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 of $10.4&nbsp;million were relatively flat compared to the prior year. </FONT></P>

June 2012 and the opening of its sports bar and buffet in August 2012. </FONT></P>

partially offset by a decrease at Mountaineer of $1.2&nbsp;million, which was primarily due to a lease bonus payment of $2.1&nbsp;million received during 2011, with no royalty payments received

compared to the prior year. The increase was primarily attributable to the opening of our gaming facility at Scioto Downs, coupled with increased offerings for our customers through the launch of the
new loyalty program during the second quarter of 2012 and increased rated play frequency at our properties. </FONT></P>

compared to the prior year. The increase of $22.9&nbsp;million is comprised of an increase in gaming taxes and assessments of $19.3&nbsp;million and other gaming operating costs of $3.5 million.
Charges of $0.4&nbsp;million and $5.9&nbsp;million, respectively, are included in 2012 and 2011 for the estimate of Presque Isle Downs proportionate assessment of amounts due under an
administrative order executed by the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board in July 2011. Excluding these gaming assessment charges in 2012 and 2011, gaming taxes increased $24.9&nbsp;million during 2012
compared to the prior year, which is consistent with the increase in gaming revenues. Gaming taxes and assessments as a percentage of gaming revenues varies by the states in which our properties
operate. On a blended basis, our gaming taxes and assessments as a percentage of gaming revenue decreased to 52.8% for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 (excluding the $0.4&nbsp;million charge
for other gaming assessment costs) compared to 54.6% (excluding the $5.9&nbsp;million charge for other gaming assessment costs) for the prior year, largely due to a lower effective gaming tax rate
of 42.5% on slots revenue at our facility at Scioto Downs. Our gaming taxes and assessments as a percentage of gaming revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 were 54.2% and 55.9%,
respectively, at Mountaineer and Presque Isle Downs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Impairment Loss  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;An impairment loss of $0.7&nbsp;million was incurred for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 due to the adjustment of the
carrying values of certain non-operating real properties. The carrying values of these properties exceeded their fair values, which were determined by independent appraisals and considered
expected net cash flows, including estimates of costs to sell. Based upon the results of the 2012 appraisals, no adjustments to the carrying values of non-operating properties were
necessary for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, we incurred a net loss on the sale or disposal of property of $0.5&nbsp;million. No
significant gains or losses resulted from the sale or disposal of property during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Interest Expense, net  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense, net increased by $7.8&nbsp;million, or 13.0%, to $67.8&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012,
compared to the prior year. The increase primarily relates to the refinancing transaction that occurred in August 2011, where we issued $565&nbsp;million of 11.5% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes
and whose proceeds were used to refinance our former debt obligations and finance development of the Scioto Downs gaming facility. The increase was partially offset by $1.3&nbsp;million in
capitalized interest incurred in 2012 as a result of the construction of our gaming facility at Scioto Downs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Loss on Debt Extinguishment  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During 2011, we incurred a loss on the extinguishment of debt in the aggregate amount of $34.4 million as a result of the repurchase of
our previous $125.0&nbsp;million Senior Subordinated Notes and $260.0&nbsp;million Senior Secured Notes on August&nbsp;1, 2011. We did not incur a similar loss during the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2012. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Income Taxes  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The income tax provision for the periods presented results in an effective tax rate that has an unusual relationship to the Company's
pretax loss. This is due to an increase in the federal and state valuation allowances on the Company's deferred tax assets as discussed below. The income tax provision also includes interest expense
related to uncertain tax positions. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
difference between the effective rate and the statutory rate is attributed primarily to permanent items not deductible for income tax purposes and the treatment of certain items in
accordance with the rules for interperiod tax allocation. As a result of our net operating losses and the net deferred tax asset position (after exclusion of certain deferred tax liabilities that
generally cannot be offset against deferred tax assets), we expect to continue to provide for a full valuation allowance against all of our net federal and net state deferred tax assets. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
income tax purposes we amortize or depreciate certain assets that have been assigned an indefinite life for book purposes. The incremental amortization or depreciation deductions for
income tax purposes result in an increase in certain deferred tax liabilities that cannot be used as a source of future taxable income for purposes of measuring our need for a valuation allowance
against the net deferred tax assets. Therefore, we expect to record non-cash deferred tax expense as we amortize these assets for tax purposes. Our tax expense was $3.6&nbsp;million and
$4.3&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 2011, respectively, and was largely the result of increases in our valuation allowances. </FONT></P>

<A NAME="toc_do44201_2"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>  <A NAME="results"></A>Financial results for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 compared to the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2010    <BR>    </I></B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="do44201_net_revenues"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_do44201_3"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B>  Net Revenues    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, comprised of $395.5&nbsp;million in gaming and pari-mutuel
revenues (92% of total net revenues), $43.7&nbsp;million of non-gaming revenues (10% of total net revenues) less $11.1&nbsp;million of promotional allowances (-2% of total
net revenues), increased $3.2&nbsp;million, or 0.8%, compared to net revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2010, comprised of $393.7&nbsp;million in gaming and pari-mutuel
revenues (92% of total net revenues), $41.0&nbsp;million of non-gaming revenues (10% of total net revenues) less $9.8&nbsp;million of promotional allowances (-2% of total
net revenues). The increase was primarily attributable to the following components. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming
revenues are comprised of the net win from our slot operations, table games and poker. Gaming revenues for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $385.3&nbsp;million
represents a $2.8&nbsp;million, or 0.7%, increase compared to the prior year. The increase of $2.8&nbsp;million is comprised of an increase in table gaming revenue of $5.8&nbsp;million, offset
by decreases in slot and poker revenue of $2.1&nbsp;million and $0.9&nbsp;million, respectively. The increase in table gaming revenue was primarily due to the introduction of table games at our
Presque Isle Downs facility in July 2010, which provided incremental gaming revenue of $10.6&nbsp;million, offset by a decrease at Mountaineer of $4.8&nbsp;million due to competitive pressures
from the commencement of table games at the Pennsylvania casinos in July 2010. The decrease in slot revenue was primarily due to road construction and traffic delays on each of the primary feeder
highways at our Presque Isle Downs facility during 2011, as well as increased competitive pressures from casinos in western Pennsylvania and western New York. The decrease in poker revenue was
primarily attributable to competitive pressures from the commencement of table games at the Pennsylvania casinos in July 2010 and at our Mountaineer facility, offset by an increase at Presque Isle
Downs due to the opening of the poker room in October 2011. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming
revenue at Mountaineer decreased by $5.9&nbsp;million, or 2.9%, to $196.8&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior year. The decrease is
comprised of a decrease in table gaming and poker revenue of $4.9&nbsp;million and $1.4&nbsp;million, respectively, offset by an increase in slot revenue of $0.4&nbsp;million. We attribute the
decreases in table gaming and poker revenue primarily to the commencement of table games at Pennsylvania casinos in July 2010, which caused an increase in competitive pressures from The Rivers Casino,
which is located in downtown Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and is approximately a one-hour drive from Mountaineer, and The Meadows Racetrack&nbsp;&amp; Casino, a harness racetrack in Washington,
Pennsylvania, which is approximately 50 miles southeast of Mountaineer, and to a lesser extent, Presque Isle Downs. We attribute the slot revenue increase to a change in Mountaineer's marketing
approach during the fourth quarter of 2011, which utilizes the entire availability of free play more effectively and provides consistent promotional offerings. The marketing approach, coupled with
milder winter weather in late-2011, brought patrons to the property on a more consistent basis than in the previous year. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming
revenue at Presque Isle Downs increased by $8.6&nbsp;million, or 4.8%, to $188.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior year. The
increase is comprised of an increase in table gaming and poker revenue of $10.6&nbsp;million and $0.5&nbsp;million, respectively, offset by a decrease in slot revenue of $2.5&nbsp;million. The
increase in table gaming revenue was due to the commencement of table gaming operations in July 2010 and the increase in poker revenue was due to the opening of the poker room in October 2011. We
attribute the decrease in slot revenues primarily to road construction and traffic delays on each of the casino's primary feeder highways during 2011, as well as increased competitive pressures from
casinos in western Pennsylvania and western New York, as discussed above. </FONT></P>

HREF="#bg44201a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Pari-Mutuel Commissions  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Pari-mutuel commissions consist of commissions earned from thoroughbred and harness racing and importing/exporting of
simulcast signals from/to other race tracks. Pari-mutuel commissions decreased by $1.0&nbsp;million, or 8.7%, to $10.2&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Pari-mutuel
commissions at Mountaineer decreased by $0.6&nbsp;million, or 9.4%, to $6.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior
year. Pari-mutuel commissions at Presque Isle Downs decreased by $0.2&nbsp;million, or 8.5%, to $2.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior
year. The decreases in pari-mutuel commissions at both Mountaineer and Presque Isle Downs were due to a decline in wagering, which is consistent with the national average decline in
wagering of 5.7% during 2011 compared to 2010, as reported by </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Equibase Company</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. Pari-mutuel commissions at Scioto Downs for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $1.4&nbsp;million represent a $0.2&nbsp;million, or 13.2%, decrease from the prior year. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Food, Beverage and Lodging  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue from our food, beverage and lodging operations for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $32.6&nbsp;million represents a
$0.3&nbsp;million, or 1.1%, increase compared to the prior year. This slight increase in food, beverage and lodging revenue was primarily attributable to an increase in patron traffic at
Mountaineer. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Food,
beverage and lodging revenue at Mountaineer increased by $0.7&nbsp;million, or 3.8%, to $21.1 million for the year December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior year. The
increase of $0.7&nbsp;million was reflective of the increase in patron traffic, as discussed above. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Food
and beverage revenue at Presque Isle Downs for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $11.1 million represents a $0.4&nbsp;million, or 3.2%, decrease from the prior year,
which was primarily due to a decrease in slot patron traffic. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Other Revenues  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other revenues are primarily derived from operations of Mountaineer's Spa, Fitness Center, retail outlets and golf course; from the
sale of programs, admission fees, and lottery tickets; from check cashing and ATM services and from special events at our entertainment and convention centers. Other revenues for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $11.1&nbsp;million represent a $2.3&nbsp;million, or 26.7%, increase compared to the prior year. The increase is comprised primarily of a $2.0&nbsp;million increase
at our Mountaineer property, which was primarily derived from lease bonus payments aggregating $2.1&nbsp;million associated with the lease of mineral rights underlying certain of Mountaineer's land
holdings. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Promotional Allowances  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Promotional allowances increased by $1.3&nbsp;million, or 13.1%, to $11.1&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011,
compared to the prior year. The increase was attributable to the increase in the maximum percentage of allowable promotional credits to be redeemed from 2% to 2<SUP>1</SUP>/<SMALL>2</SMALL>% by the West Virginia
Lottery Commission during the fourth quarter of 2010, in addition to the commencement of table gaming operations in July 2010 at our Presque Isle Downs facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="do44201_operating_expenses_1"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_do44201_4"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Operating Expenses    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Gaming  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming expense for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $244.3&nbsp;million represents a $4.9&nbsp;million, or 2.0%, increase
compared to the prior year. The increase of $4.9&nbsp;million is comprised of an increase </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>41</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- ZEQ.=5,SEQ=41,EFW="2213661",CP="MTR GAMING GROUP, INC.",DN="1",CHK=493515,FOLIO='41',FILE='DISK133:[13ZAB1.13ZAB44201]DO44201A.;11',USER='MSULLIV',CD='14-MAR-2013;17:25' -->

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>in
gaming taxes and assessments of $3.3&nbsp;million and other gaming operating costs of $1.6&nbsp;million. The third quarter of 2011 includes a $5.9&nbsp;million charge for the estimate of
Presque Isle Downs proportionate assessment of amounts due under an administrative order executed by the Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board in July 2011. Additionally, the third quarter of 2010
includes a one-time assessment fee of $0.8&nbsp;million for Presque Isle Downs, which is required of each slot machine licensee after commencement of gaming operations. Excluding these
gaming assessment charges in both 2011 and 2010, gaming taxes decreased $1.8&nbsp;million during 2011 compared to the prior year. Mountaineer's gaming taxes and assessments decreased by
$2.0&nbsp;million during 2011 compared to 2010 as a result of the overall decrease in gaming revenues. Even though gaming revenues at Presque Isle Downs increased by $8.6&nbsp;million during 2011
compared to 2010, gaming taxes and assessments (excluding the regulatory gaming assessment costs incurred in both 2011 and 2010) only increased overall by $0.2&nbsp;million to $105.0&nbsp;million
compared to 2010. This slight increase resulted from the $11.2&nbsp;million increase in table gaming revenue, offset by the $2.5&nbsp;million decrease in slot revenue, which has a much higher tax
rate. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming
taxes and assessments as a percentage of gaming revenues varies by the states in which our properties operate. On a blended basis, our gaming taxes and assessments as a percentage
of gaming revenue decreased to 54.6% (excluding the $5.9&nbsp;million charge for other gaming assessment costs) for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 compared to 55.5% (excluding the
$0.8&nbsp;million charge for other gaming assessment costs) for the prior year, largely due to the overall decrease in table gaming and poker revenue at Mountaineer. Our gaming taxes and assessments
as a percentage of gaming revenue for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 were 53.5% and 55.7%, respectively, at Mountaineer and Presque Isle Downs (excluding the $5.9&nbsp;million charge for
other gaming assessment costs). </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Pari-Mutuel  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Pari-mutuel expense of $11.4&nbsp;million represents a $0.1&nbsp;million, or 1.2%, increase compared to the prior year. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Food, Beverage and Lodging  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Food, beverage and lodging expense increased by $0.4&nbsp;million, or 1.9%, to $23.7&nbsp;million for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior year. The increase was primarily due to the increase in food, beverage and lodging revenues. Our gross profit margin for the
year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 decreased to 27.3% from 27.9% in the prior year. The gross profit margin was primarily impacted by a 2% increase in food costs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Other  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other expense increased by $0.1&nbsp;million, or 2.1%, to $6.3&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared
to the prior year. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Marketing and Promotions  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Marketing and promotions expense decreased by $0.2&nbsp;million, or 1.4%, to $12.6&nbsp;million for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the prior year. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> General and Administrative  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;General and administrative expense decreased by $1.1&nbsp;million, or 2.0%, to $53.0&nbsp;million for the year ended
December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to the period year. Significant factors contributing to the decrease in general and administrative expenses were:</FONT></P>

<UL>
<DL compact>
<DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>the absence of severance costs of $1.1&nbsp;million during 2011 that related to the resignations of executives during
the third quarter of 2010; </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>a decrease in legal, lobbying costs and other outside services of $0.9&nbsp;million during 2011 compared to 2010; </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>a decrease in salaries, bonuses and benefits of $0.5&nbsp;million during 2011 compared to 2010; </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>an increase of $0.9&nbsp;million at Presque Isle Downs, which is primarily attributable to an increase in compensation
and benefits as a result of the implementation of table games and poker; and </FONT><FONT SIZE=2>
<BR><BR></FONT></DD><DT style='font-family:times;margin-bottom:-11pt;'><FONT SIZE=2>&#149;</FONT></DT><DD style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>an increase in long-term incentive plan compensation in the amount of $0.6&nbsp;million during 2011 compared
to 2010. </FONT></DD></DL>
</UL>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Project Opening Costs  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Project opening costs decreased by $1.2&nbsp;million, or 85.6%, to $0.2&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011
compared to the prior year. The decrease was due to the absence of project-opening costs of $1.4&nbsp;million during 2010 related to the implementation of table games at our Presque Isle Downs
gaming facility. The costs for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 of $0.2&nbsp;million were related to the opening of the poker room at our Presque Isle Downs gaming facility in October 2011
and to a lesser extent, the Scioto Downs VLT gaming facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Depreciation  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Depreciation expense decreased by $0.8&nbsp;million, or 2.8%, to $27.9&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011,
compared to the prior year. The decrease was attributed to a $1.6&nbsp;million decrease in depreciation expense at Mountaineer due to the aging of assets, offset by an $0.8&nbsp;million increase
at Presque Isle Downs as a result of increased capital expenditures due to the implementation of table games in 2010. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Impairment Loss  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;An impairment loss of $0.7&nbsp;million was incurred for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011 due to the adjustment of the
carrying values of certain non-operating real properties. The carrying values of these properties exceeded their fair values, which were determined by independent appraisals and considered
expected net cash flows, including estimates of costs to sell. Based upon the results of the 2010 appraisals, no adjustments to the carrying values of non-operating properties were
necessary for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2010. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Loss on the sale or disposal of property  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Loss on the sale or disposal of property increased by $0.4&nbsp;million to $0.5&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31,
2011, compared to the prior year. The increase is primarily attributed to a loss of $0.7&nbsp;million incurred in 2011 as a result of an unfavorable ruling in December 2011 in relation to Presque
Isle Downs' sale of non-operating property to the Greater Erie Industrial Development Corporation in 2005, partially offset by a gain of $0.2&nbsp;million incurred in 2011 due to the
sale of 21 acres of non-operating real property by Mountaineer. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Interest Expense, net  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Interest expense, net increased by $5.9&nbsp;million, or 11.0%, to $60.0&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011,
compared to the prior year. The increase primarily relates to the refinancing transaction that occurred in August 2011, where we issued $565&nbsp;million of 11.5% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes
and whose proceeds were used to refinance our former debt obligations and finance development of the Scioto Downs gaming facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Loss on Debt Extinguishment  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the third quarter of 2011, we incurred a loss on the extinguishment of debt in the aggregate amount of $34.4&nbsp;million as a
result of the repurchase of our previous $125.0&nbsp;million Senior Subordinated Notes and $260.0&nbsp;million Senior Secured Notes on August&nbsp;1, 2011. The loss reflects the
write-off of the net unamortized deferred financing fees associated with the aforementioned notes, as well as with our former credit facility, in the aggregate amount of
$9.8&nbsp;million, the write-off of net unamortized original issue discount related to our previous $260&nbsp;million Senior Secured Notes in the amount of $7.4&nbsp;million, and the
payment of tender or redemption fees to the holders of the aforementioned notes in the aggregate amount of $17.2&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Income Taxes  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The income tax provision for the periods presented results in an effective tax rate that has an unusual relationship to the Company's
pretax loss. This is due to an increase in the federal and state valuation allowances on the Company's deferred tax assets as discussed below. The income tax provision also includes interest expense
related to uncertain tax positions. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
difference between the effective rate and the statutory rate is attributed primarily to permanent items not deductible for income tax purposes and the treatment of certain items in
accordance with the rules for interperiod tax allocation. As a result of our net operating losses and the net deferred tax asset position (after exclusion of certain deferred tax liabilities that
generally cannot be offset against deferred tax assets), we expect to continue to provide for a full valuation allowance against all of our net federal and net state deferred tax assets. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
income tax purposes we amortize or depreciate certain assets that have been assigned an indefinite life for book purposes. The incremental amortization or depreciation deductions for
income tax purposes result in an increase in certain deferred tax liabilities that cannot be used as a source of future taxable income for purposes of measuring our need for a valuation allowance
against the net deferred tax assets. Therefore, we expect to record non-cash deferred tax expense as we amortize these assets for tax purposes. Our tax expense was $4.3&nbsp;million for
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, compared to a tax benefit of $1.4&nbsp;million for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2010. The increase in tax expense was largely the result of increases
in our valuation allowances. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="do44201_property_adjusted_ebitda"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_do44201_5"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Property Adjusted EBITDA    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Adjusted EBITDA (defined below), a non-GAAP financial measure, has been presented as a supplemental disclosure because it
is a widely used measure of performance and basis for valuation of companies in our industry. Management of the Company uses Adjusted EBITDA as the primary measure of the Company's operating
performance and as a component in evaluating the performance of operating personnel. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Adjusted
EBITDA represents (losses) earnings before interest expense (income), income tax expense (benefit), depreciation and amortization, (loss) gain on the sale or disposal of
property, other regulatory gaming assessment costs, loss on asset impairment, loss (gain) on debt modification and extinguishment and equity in loss on unconsolidated joint venture, to the extent that
such items existed in the periods presented. Adjusted EBITDA is not a measure of performance or liquidity calculated in accordance with GAAP, is unaudited and should not be considered an alternative
to, or more meaningful than, net income (loss) as an indicator of our operating performance, or cash flows from operating activities, as a measure of liquidity. Uses of cash flows that are not
reflected in Adjusted EBITDA include capital expenditures, interest payments, income taxes, debt principal repayments and certain regulatory gaming assessments, which can be significant. Other
companies that provide EBITDA information may calculate EBITDA differently than we do. The definition of Adjusted EBITDA may not be the same as the definitions used in any of our debt agreements. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="dq44201_liquidity_and_sources_of_capital"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_dq44201_1"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Liquidity and Sources of Capital    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The primary sources of liquidity and capital resources have been existing cash, cash flow from operations and proceeds from the
issuance of debt securities. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At
December&nbsp;31, 2012, our cash and cash equivalents, excluding restricted cash, totaled $115.1&nbsp;million. As of December&nbsp;31, 2012, Mountaineer has contributed funds
for racing purses, which exceed our purse payment obligations by $6.3&nbsp;million. This amount is available for payment of future purse obligations at our discretion, and is held in bank accounts
owned by the horsemen's association. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;At
December&nbsp;31, 2012, we had total debt in the aggregate principal amount of $556.7&nbsp;million; net of discounts, all of which was secured, and cash collateralized letters of
credit of approximately $0.2&nbsp;million were outstanding. In connection with the August 2011 refinancing transaction, we entered into a $20.0&nbsp;million senior secured revolving credit
facility. At December&nbsp;31, 2012, there were no borrowings under the credit facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
believe that our cash balances on hand, cash flow from operations, availability under the credit facility and any proceeds from the sale of non-core assets will be
sufficient to fund our liquidity needs, including debt service of our Senior Secured Second Lien Notes, any other
contemplated capital expenditures and short-term funding requirements for the next twelve months, as well as the amounts required for the remaining licensing related to Scioto Downs. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
cannot assure you that estimates of our liquidity needs are accurate or that new business developments or other unforeseen events will not occur. If any of these events occur, it may
require additional liquidity to continue to execute our business strategy. We anticipate that, to the extent that we require additional liquidity, it will be funded through the incurrence of
indebtedness, equity offerings or a combination of potential sources of liquidity, although no assurance can be given that such forms of capital will be available to us or available to us on terms
which are acceptable, at such time. </FONT></P>

 <P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Operating Cash Flow  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net cash provided by operating activities approximated $45.1&nbsp;million during 2012 compared to $39.7&nbsp;million during 2011.
The increase is primarily due to an increase in operating income as the result of the opening of our gaming facility at Scioto Downs in June 2012. Current period non-cash expenses included
in operating activities, consisting primarily of depreciation and amortization, were $35.9&nbsp;million. In 2011, non-cash expenses included $39.5&nbsp;million consisting primarily of
depreciation and amortization and $34.4&nbsp;million in write-offs of deferred financing and other fees resulting from the extinguishment of long-term debt. Additionally, net
cash provided by operating activities included changes in operating assets and liabilities of $15.0&nbsp;million during the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012. During 2011, net cash provided by
operating activities included changes in operating assets and liabilities of $16.2&nbsp;million, due primarily to an increase in accrued interest. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Investing Cash Flow  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net cash used in investing activities was $15.4&nbsp;million during 2012, comprised primarily of capital expenditures of
$119.1&nbsp;million and a $25.0&nbsp;million payment of the Ohio video lottery terminal license fee, offset by the use of funds held for construction in the amount of $130.1&nbsp;million. During
2011, net cash used in investing activities was $139.1&nbsp;million, comprised primarily of $130.1&nbsp;million of funds held for construction, capital expenditures aggregating
$11.3&nbsp;million offset by the reimbursement of capital expenditures from West Virginia regulatory authorities aggregating $1.8&nbsp;million, and proceeds from the sale of property aggregating
$0.5&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Financing Cash Flow  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Net cash used in financing activities was $0.2&nbsp;million during 2012 compared to net cash provided by financing activities of
$131.1&nbsp;million during 2011. Financing activities for 2012 included the payment of financing costs of $0.2&nbsp;million. Financing activities for 2011 included net proceeds of
$548.1&nbsp;million from the issuance of $565&nbsp;million of our Senior Secured Second Lien Notes which were utilized to repurchase our previously issued $125&nbsp;million Senior Subordinated
Notes for $125.2&nbsp;million, repurchase our previously issued $260&nbsp;million Senior Secured Notes for $277.0&nbsp;million, and pay various financing-related costs aggregating
$12.8&nbsp;million. Other principal payments on long-term obligations aggregated $1.9&nbsp;million in 2011. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, cash flows from operating and financing activities excludes $5.7&nbsp;million, which represents the portion of the interest payable on
the Senior Secured Lien Notes that was satisfied with PIK Notes on February&nbsp;1 and August&nbsp;1, 2012. </FONT></P>

<A NAME="toc_dq44201_3"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Capital Expenditures    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, additions to property and equipment and other capital projects aggregated
$114.9&nbsp;million, which included $106.7&nbsp;million related to the VLT gaming facility at Scioto Downs, $2.2&nbsp;million to the construction of three new barns at Presque Isle Downs,
$3.3&nbsp;million for new slot machines at all three properties, and $1.2&nbsp;million for renovations at Mountaineer. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;During
the third quarter of 2012, we completed the final phase of construction on our gaming facility at Scioto Downs. Development, construction and equipment costs are expected to be
approximately $125.0&nbsp;million over a required three-year period. During the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, we expended approximately $106.7&nbsp;million related to the
construction costs and equipment purchases, including $1.2&nbsp;million of capitalized interest. Of the required total $125.0&nbsp;million project investment, we have expended a total of
approximately $111.7&nbsp;million for construction and equipment related costs, including $1.3&nbsp;million of capitalized interest, through December&nbsp;31, 2012. The project also included
certain other development related expenditures, for which a determination has not been made as to whether such costs will be included in satisfying the investment requirement. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Under
legislation approved by West Virginia in July 2011, Mountaineer participates in a modernization fund which provides for reimbursement from amounts paid to the West Virginia Lottery
Commission, of $1 for each $2 expended for certain qualifying capital expenditures having a useful life of more than three years and placed into service after July&nbsp;1, 2011. Qualifying capital
expenditures include the purchase of slot machines and related equipment to the extent such slot machines are retained by Mountaineer at its West Virginia location for not less than five years. In
July 2011, the West Virginia Lottery Commission issued an administrative order which stated that approximately $3.7&nbsp;million would be available to Mountaineer during the state's fiscal year
commencing July&nbsp;1, 2011. Any unexpended balance from a given fiscal year will be available for one additional fiscal year, after which time the remaining unused balance carried forward will be
forfeited. During 2012, Mountaineer made purchases aggregating $1.5&nbsp;million, which qualified for reimbursement under the modernization fund of approximately $0.8&nbsp;million, all of which we
received during 2012. In addition, during the six months ended December&nbsp;31, 2011, Mountaineer made eligible purchases aggregating $3.0&nbsp;million, which qualified for a reimbursement of
approximately $1.5&nbsp;million. Through December&nbsp;31, 2011, we received $1.4&nbsp;million and the remaining $0.1&nbsp;million was received during the first quarter of 2012. As of
December&nbsp;31, 2012, approximately $1.4&nbsp;million of the initial $3.7&nbsp;million allocated to Mountaineer remains available, and we anticipate we will be able to receive these funds
through qualifying capital expenditures to be made prior to the fiscal year 2011 modernization fund's expiration in June 2013. Additionally, we have received notification from the West Virginia
Lottery Commission that Mountaineer is now eligible for another estimated $3.7&nbsp;million of reimbursement from the modernization fund, effective July&nbsp;1, 2012 through June&nbsp;30, 2014. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
anticipate spending up to a total of approximately $19.3&nbsp;million during 2013 on capital expenditures. Expenditures for 2013 are expected to include $8.6&nbsp;million for slot
machines, $6.2&nbsp;million for other
gaming floor enhancements, $1.5&nbsp;million for hotel renovations, $1.5&nbsp;million for IT related expenses and $1.5&nbsp;million for other related capital expenditures. We also anticipate
receiving reimbursement from West Virginia of approximately $2.2&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Debt    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Credit Facility  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On August&nbsp;1, 2011, we entered into a senior secured revolving credit facility (the "Credit Facility") with a borrowing
availability of $20.0&nbsp;million and a maturity date of August&nbsp;1, 2016. The interest rate per annum applicable to loans under the Credit Facility will be, at the Company's option, either
(i)&nbsp;LIBOR plus a spread of 4.0%, or (ii)&nbsp;base rate, which will be the "prime rate" of interest in effect </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>49</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>on
the day of the borrowing request as published in the Wall Street Journal, plus a spread of 3.0%. There were no borrowings outstanding at December&nbsp;31, 2012. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Credit Facility is secured by substantially the same assets securing the 11.5% Senior Secured Second Lien Notes (the "Notes"), discussed below (and including securities of the
Company's subsidiaries to the extent permitted by law). Borrowings under the Credit Facility are guaranteed by all of our existing and future domestic restricted subsidiaries. The security interest in
the collateral that secures the Credit Facility is senior to the security interest in the collateral that secures the Notes. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Credit Facility contains a number of customary covenants that, among other things, restrict, subject to certain exceptions, our ability and the ability of our subsidiary guarantors
to incur additional indebtedness or become a guarantor; create a lien on collateral; engage in mergers, consolidations or asset dispositions; pay dividends or make distributions; make investments,
loans or advances; engage in certain transactions with affiliates or subsidiaries; make capital expenditures; or modify our line of
business. The Credit Facility also includes certain financial covenants, including the requirements that the Company maintain throughout the term of the Credit Facility and measured as of the end of
each fiscal quarter (on a trailing four-quarter period basis), the following maximum consolidated leverage ratios: (i)&nbsp;7.50:1.00 for the fiscal quarter ending December&nbsp;31,
2012, (ii)&nbsp;7.00:1.00 for the fiscal quarters ending March&nbsp;31, 2013 through September&nbsp;30, 2013, and (iii)&nbsp;6.50:1.00 for the fiscal quarters ending December&nbsp;31, 2013
through December&nbsp;31, 2015. In addition, the Company will be required to maintain a minimum consolidated interest coverage ratio not greater than: (i)&nbsp;1.40:1.00 for the fiscal quarters
ending December&nbsp;31, 2012 through December&nbsp;31, 2015 and a minimum consolidated EBITDA amount of (x)&nbsp;$60.0&nbsp;million for the fiscal quarter ending December&nbsp;31, 2012 and
(y)&nbsp;$80.0&nbsp;million for the fiscal quarters ending March&nbsp;31, 2013 through December&nbsp;31, 2015. Capital expenditures are also limited to $25.0&nbsp;million per annum
throughout the term of the Credit Facility. As of December&nbsp;31, 2012, the Company remained in compliance with the covenants. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Permitted
indebtedness under the Credit Facility includes furniture and equipment financing provided that the aggregate principal amounts of such indebtedness outstanding at any time
shall not exceed the greater of $20.0&nbsp;million and 4.5% of consolidated net tangible assets, as defined; other unsecured indebtedness at any time not to exceed $5.0&nbsp;million; and other
indebtedness to finance the acquisition, development or construction of any future gaming property provided that (i)&nbsp;such indebtedness shall be unsecured and subordinated to the Credit
Facility, (ii)&nbsp;no part of the principal or interest of such indebtedness is required to be paid prior to six months after the maturity date of the Credit Facility and (iii)&nbsp;upon the
incurrence of such indebtedness and after giving pro forma effect thereto there shall be no default or event of default and that we shall be in pro forma compliance with the financial covenants. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><I> Senior Secured Second Lien Notes  </I></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;On August&nbsp;1, 2011, we completed the offering of $565.0&nbsp;million in aggregate principal amount of 11.5% Senior Secured
Second Lien Notes due August&nbsp;1, 2019 at an issue price equal to 97% of the aggregate principal amount of the Notes. The net proceeds of the sale of the Notes were utilized to refinance our
former debt obligations and to finance development of the Scioto Downs gaming facility. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Notes will mature on August&nbsp;1, 2019, with interest payable semi-annually in arrears on February&nbsp;1 and August&nbsp;1 of each year. Until and including the
interest payment due on August&nbsp;1, 2013, interest could have been payable, at the election of the Company, (i)&nbsp;entirely in cash or (ii)&nbsp;at a rate of 10.50% in cash and a rate of
1.00% paid in kind ("PIK") by increasing the principal amount of the outstanding Notes or by issuing additional PIK Notes, as defined in the Indenture. The interest payments due on February&nbsp;1
and August&nbsp;1, 2012 were satisfied in cash and PIK Notes, as defined in the Indenture. As a result, in aggregate, additional Notes of $5.6&nbsp;million were issued. We have made the election
to satisfy our February&nbsp;1, 2013 and August&nbsp;1, 2013 interest payments entirely in cash. </FONT></P>

guarantee the Notes. </FONT></P>

to the date of purchase with 75% of our excess cash flow in excess of $7.5&nbsp;million for such fiscal year. As of December&nbsp;31, 2012, no excess cash flow purchase offer is required to be
made in 2013. In addition, if imposed by gaming laws and regulations, the Notes are subject to redemption by the Company if after determination by applicable gaming regulatory authorities that a
holder of the Notes will not be licensed, qualified or found suitable under applicable gaming laws. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board (the "PGCB"), the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue and the Pennsylvania State Police
(collectively "the Borrowers"), were required to fund the costs they incurred in connection with the initial development of the infrastructure to support gaming operations in Pennsylvania as well as
the initial ongoing costs of the Borrowers. The initial funding of these costs was provided from a loan from the Pennsylvania General Fund in the amount of approximately $36.1&nbsp;million, and
further funding was provided from additional loans from the Pennsylvania Property Tax Reserve Fund in the aggregate amount of approximately $63.8&nbsp;million. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
Pennsylvania Department of Revenue will assess all licensees, including Presque Isle Downs, their proportionate share of amounts represented by the borrowings, which are in the
aggregate amount of $99.9&nbsp;million, once the designated number of Pennsylvania's slot machine licensees is operational. On July&nbsp;11, 2011, the PGCB issued an administrative order which
established that payments associated with the $63.8&nbsp;million that was borrowed from the Property Tax Reserve Fund would commence on January&nbsp;1, 2012. The repayment allocation between all
current licensees is based upon equal weighting of (i)&nbsp;cumulative gross slot revenue since inception in relation to the combined cumulative gross slot revenue for all licensees and
(ii)&nbsp;single year gross slot revenue (during the state's fiscal year ending June&nbsp;30) in relation to the combined single year gross slot revenue for all licensees; and amounts paid each
year will be adjusted annually based upon changes in the licensee's proportionate share of gross slot revenue. We have estimated that our total proportionate share of the aggregate
$63.8&nbsp;million to be assessed to the gaming facilities will be approximately $4.0&nbsp;million and will be paid quarterly over a ten-year period, which began effective
January&nbsp;1, 2012. For the $36.1&nbsp;million that was borrowed from the General Fund, payment is scheduled to begin after all fourteen licensees are operational. Although we cannot determine
when payment will begin, we have </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="ds44201_critical_accounting_policies"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_ds44201_4"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Critical Accounting Policies    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our significant accounting policies are included in Note&nbsp;2 to our consolidated financial statements, which is included elsewhere
in this report. These policies, along with the underlying assumptions and judgments made by our management in their application, have a significant impact on our consolidated financial statements.
These judgments are subject to an inherent degree of uncertainty and actual results could differ from our estimates. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Revenue Recognition.</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Gaming revenues consist of the net win from gaming activities, which is the difference between amounts
wagered and amounts paid
to winning patrons, and is recognized at the time wagers are made net of winning payouts to patrons. Base and progressive jackpots are accrued and charged to revenue at the time the obligation to pay
the jackpot is established. Pari-mutuel commissions consist of commissions earned from thoroughbred and harness racing, and importing of simulcast signals from other race tracks.
Pari-mutuel commissions are recognized at the time wagers are made. Such commissions are a designated portion of the wagering handle as determined by state racing commissions, and are
shown net of the taxes assessed by state and local agencies, as well as purses and other contractual amounts paid to horsemen associations. We recognize revenues from fees earned through the exporting
of simulcast signals to other race tracks at the time wagers are made. Such fees are based upon a predetermined percentage
of handle as contracted with the other race tracks. Revenues from food and beverage are recognized at the time of sale and revenues from lodging are recognized on the date of stay. Other revenues are
recorded at the time services are rendered or merchandise sold. We offer certain promotional allowances to our customers, including complimentary lodging, food and beverage, and promotional credits
for free play on slot machines. The retail value of these promotional items is shown as a reduction in total revenues on our consolidated statements of operations. </FONT></P>


<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Impairment of Other Indefinite-Lived Intangible Assets.</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We review the carrying value of our indefinite-lived intangible assets no
less than annually.
Unforeseen events, changes in circumstances and market conditions and material differences in estimates of future cash flows could negatively affect the fair value of our assets and result in an
impairment charge. Fair value is the amount at which the asset could be bought or sold in a current transaction between willing parties. Fair value can be estimated utilizing a number of techniques
including quoted market prices, prices for comparable assets, or other valuation processes involving estimates of cash flows, multiples of earnings or revenues. Management must make various
assumptions and estimates when performing its impairment assessments, particularly as it relates to cash flows and asset performance. Cash flow estimates are, by their nature, subjective and actual
results may differ materially from the estimates. Cash flow estimates include assumptions regarding factors such as recent and budgeted operating performance, net win per unit (revenue), patron
visits, growth percentages, operating margins, and current regulatory, social and economic </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>54</FONT></P>

<HR NOSHADE>
<P style='font-family:times;page-break-before:always'></p>
<!-- ZEQ.=4,SEQ=54,EFW="2213661",CP="MTR GAMING GROUP, INC.",DN="1",CHK=230926,FOLIO='54',FILE='DISK133:[13ZAB1.13ZAB44201]DS44201A.;8',USER='MSULLIV',CD='14-MAR-2013;17:25' -->
<A NAME="page_ds44201_1_55"> </A>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
HREF="#bg44201a_main_toc">Table of Contents</A></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>climates.
These estimates could also be negatively impacted by changes in federal, state, or local regulations, economic downturns or developments, other market conditions affecting travel and access
to the properties. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The
fair value measurements employed for our impairment evaluations of other indefinite-lived intangible assets were generally based on a discounted cash flow approach and review of
market data, which falls within Level&nbsp;3 of the fair value hierarchy. In accordance with the requirements of ASC 350, </FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Intangibles&#151;Goodwill and
Other</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>, we performed the annual impairment tests of our other indefinite-lived intangible assets as of December&nbsp;31, 2012. For the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and
2011, we determined that was no impairment of other indefinite-lived intangible assets based upon results of impairment evaluations. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Impairment of Property and Equipment.</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Property, equipment and other long-lived assets are assessed for impairment in accordance
with ASC
360&#151;</FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Property, Plant, and Equipment</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. For assets to be disposed of, impairment is recognized based on the lower of carrying value or fair
value less costs of disposal, as estimated based on comparable asset sales, offers received, or a
discounted cash flow model. Assets to be held and used are reviewed for impairment whenever indicators of impairment exist. The estimated future cash flows of the asset, on an undiscounted basis, are
compared to the carrying value of the asset. If the undiscounted cash flows exceed the carrying value, no impairment is indicated. If the undiscounted cash flows do not exceed the carrying value, then
an impairment is recorded based on the fair value of the asset, typically measured using a discounted cash flow model (Level&nbsp;3). </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
undeveloped properties, including non-operating real properties, when indicators of impairment are present, properties are evaluated for impairment and losses are
recorded when undiscounted cash flows estimated to be generated by an asset or market comparisons are less than the asset's carrying amount. The amount of the impairment loss is calculated as the
excess of the asset's carrying value over its fair value, which is determined using a discounted cash flow analysis, management estimates or market comparisons. The fair value measurements employed
for our impairment evaluations, which are subject to the assumptions and factors as previously discussed, were generally based on a review of comparable activities in the marketplace, which falls
within Level&nbsp;3 of the fair value hierarchy. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;For
each of the three years in the period ended December&nbsp;31, 2012, we had substantially all non-operating real properties appraised by an independent appraisal
company. Based upon the results of the 2012 appraisals, no adjustments to the carrying values of non-operating real properties were necessary for the year ended December&nbsp;31, 2012.
We do not anticipate that we will be able to sell the majority of these assets within the next twelve months. As such, these properties are not classified as held-for-sale as
of December&nbsp;31, 2012. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Frequent Players Program.</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We offer programs whereby our participating patrons can accumulate points for wagering that can be
redeemed for credits for
free play on slot machines, lodging, food and beverage, merchandise and in limited situations, cash. Based upon the estimated redemptions of frequent player program points, an estimated liability is
established for the cost of redemption on earned but unredeemed points. The estimated cost of redemption utilizes estimates and assumptions of the mix of the various product offerings for which the
points will be redeemed and costs of such product offerings. Changes in the programs, membership levels and redemption patterns of our participating patrons can impact this liability. The aggregate
outstanding liability for the frequent players program was $0.7&nbsp;million and $0.6&nbsp;million at December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 2011, respectively, and is included as a component of other
accrued liabilities in our accompanying consolidated balance sheets. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Income Taxes.</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We compute our annual tax rate based on the statutory tax rates and tax planning opportunities available to us in
the various
jurisdictions in which we earn income. Significant judgment </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>is
required in determining our annual tax rate and in evaluating uncertainty in our tax positions. We recognize a benefit for tax positions that we believe will more likely than not be sustained upon
examination. The amount of benefit recognized is the largest amount of benefit that we believe has more than a 50% probability of being realized upon settlement. We regularly monitor our tax positions
and adjust the amount of recognized tax benefit based on our evaluation of information that has become available since the end of our last financial reporting period. The annual tax rate includes the
impact of these changes in recognized tax benefits. The difference between the amount of benefit taken or expected to be taken in a tax return and the amount of benefit recognized for financial
reporting represents unrecognized tax benefits. These unrecognized tax benefits are presented in the balance sheet principally within accrued income taxes. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We
record valuation allowances to reduce deferred tax assets to the amount that is more likely than not to be realized. When assessing the need for valuation allowances, we consider
future taxable income and ongoing prudent and feasible tax planning strategies. Should a change in circumstances lead to a change in judgment about the realizability of deferred tax assets in future
years, we would adjust related valuation allowances in the period that the change in circumstances occurs, along with a corresponding increase or charge to income. As of December&nbsp;31, 2012, we
have valuation allowances aggregating $27.4&nbsp;million, principally related to certain federal and state net operating loss carryforwards. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><B><I> &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Stock-Based Compensation.</I></B></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We account for stock-based compensation in accordance with
ASC&nbsp;718&#151;</FONT><FONT SIZE=2><I>Compensation&#151;Stock Compensation</I></FONT><FONT SIZE=2>. ASC 718 requires all share-based payments to employees, including grants of
employee stock options and restricted stock units, to be recognized in the consolidated statement of operations based on their fair values and that compensation expense be recognized for awards over
the requisite service period of the award or to an employee's eligible retirement date, if earlier. Determining the fair value of stock-based awards at the grant date requires judgment, including
estimating the expected term that stock options will be outstanding prior to exercise and the associated volatility. We used the simplified method for estimating expected option life and historic
volatility for estimating volatility. During the years ended December&nbsp;31, 2012 and 2011, we recorded stock-based compensation expense of $1.1&nbsp;million and $0.9&nbsp;million,
respectively. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="ds44201_recently_issued_accounting_pronouncements"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_ds44201_5"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Recently Issued Accounting Pronouncements    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In February 2013, the Financial Accounting Standards Board ("FASB") issued new accounting guidance for the reporting of amounts
reclassified out of accumulated other
comprehensive income. The amendment requires an entity to report the effect of significant reclassifications out of accumulated other comprehensive income on the respective line items in net income if
the amount being reclassified is required under GAAP to be reclassified in its entirety to net income. For other amounts that are not required under GAAP to be reclassified in their entirety to net
income in the same reporting period, an entity is required to cross-reference other disclosures required under GAAP that provide additional detail about those amounts. This would be the case when a
portion of the amount reclassified out of accumulated other comprehensive income is reclassified to a balance sheet account instead of directly to income or expense in the same reporting period. The
new guidance is effective prospectively for reporting periods beginning after December&nbsp;15, 2012. We do not expect the adoption of this guidance to have a material impact on our financial
position, results of operations or cash flows. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Other
pronouncements issued by the FASB or other authoritative accounting standards groups with future effective dates are either not applicable or are not expected to be significant to
our financial position, results of operations or cash flows. </FONT></P>

<A NAME="toc_ds44201_9"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B>  ITEM 9A.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;CONTROLS AND PROCEDURES.    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="ds44201_evaluation_of_disclosure_controls_and_procedures"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_ds44201_10"> </A></FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><B>  Evaluation of Disclosure Controls and Procedures    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;We have established and maintain disclosure controls and procedures that are designed to ensure that information required to be
disclosed in our reports that we file under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act"), is recorded, processed, summarized, evaluated and reported within the time periods
specified in the rules and forms of the Securities and Exchange Commission, and that such information is accumulated and communicated to management, including our Chief Executive Officer and Chief
Financial Officer, as appropriate to allow timely decisions regarding required disclosure. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In
designing and evaluating the disclosure controls and procedures, management recognized that any controls and procedures, no matter how well designed and operated, can provide only
reasonable assurance of achieving the desired control objectives, and management necessarily was required to apply its judgment in evaluating the cost-benefit relationship of possible
controls and procedures. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our
Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer evaluated the effectiveness of our disclosure controls and procedures (as defined in Exchange Act
Rules&nbsp;13a-15(e) and 15d-15(e)) as of December&nbsp;31, 2012. They have concluded that our disclosure controls and procedures are effective to ensure that the
information required to be disclosed by us in the reports that we file under the Exchange Act is recorded, processed, summarized, evaluated and reported within the time periods specified in SEC rules
and forms. </FONT></P>

<P ALIGN="CENTER" style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>57</FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="ds44201_management_s_report_on_interna__man02650"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_ds44201_11"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Management's Report on Internal Control over Financial Reporting    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Our management is responsible for establishing and maintaining adequate internal control over financial reporting (as defined in
Exchange Act Rule&nbsp;13a-15(f)). There are inherent limitations in the effectiveness of any internal control over financial reporting, including the possibility of human error and the
circumvention or overriding of controls. Also, projections of any evaluation of effectiveness to future periods are subject to the risk that controls may become inadequate because of changes in
conditions, or that the degree of compliance with the policies and procedures may deteriorate. Accordingly, our internal controls over financial reporting is designed to provide reasonable assurance
regarding the reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Management
conducted an evaluation and assessed the effectiveness of our internal control over financial reporting as of December&nbsp;31, 2012, based upon the framework in </FONT> <FONT SIZE=2><I>Internal Control&#151;Integrated Framework</I></FONT><FONT
SIZE=2> issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO). Based on our
evaluation and assessment, our management concluded that our internal control over financial reporting was effective as of December&nbsp;31, 2012, to provide reasonable assurance regarding
reliability of financial reporting and the preparation of financial statements for external purposes in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Ernst&nbsp;&amp;
Young&nbsp;LLP, the independent registered public accounting firm that audited the Company's consolidated financial statements included in this
Form&nbsp;10-K, has issued an attestation report on the Company's internal control over financial reporting. Ernst&nbsp;&amp; Young&nbsp;LLP's attestation report on the Company's
internal control over financial reporting is included in this Form&nbsp;10-K. </FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2><A
NAME="ds44201_changes_in_internal_controls"> </A>
<A NAME="toc_ds44201_12"> </A>
<BR></FONT><FONT SIZE=2><B>  Changes in Internal Controls    <BR>    </B></FONT></P>

<P style="font-family:times;"><FONT SIZE=2>&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;There were no significant changes in our internal control over financial reporting that occurred during the last fiscal quarter ended
December&nbsp;31, 2012 that have materially affected, or are reasonably likely to materially affect, our internal control over financial reporting. </FONT></P>
